info.title: Midori Native Sync API
info.description: Implemented native-client profile of the Laravel API. Experimental: capabilities currently announce native_ready=false. This document covers pairing, public-client OIDC exchange, session identity/renewal/revocation, incremental collections and native key lifecycle. The retired extension API has been removed. Send Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json for JSON bodies. Byte limits are UTF-8 byte limits, not JSON Schema character counts. See native-sync-api.md for transaction and migration semantics.

post.summary: Consume a code and create a native device session
post.description: Device names do not reuse device identity. Issuer binding is checked before consuming the code. native_refresh=true explicitly opts into version-1 renewable sessions (maximum 32 unexpired families per account); otherwise the original access-only behavior is preserved. No native OAuth/PKCE flow is implemented by this route.

Cache-Control.description: no-store on successful native data responses and protocol errors.

post.summary: Create a renewable native session after public-client OIDC authorization
post.description: The Desktop client completes authorization code with PKCE at the configured Authentik provider. This endpoint verifies the signed ID token, its issuer, public-client audience and nonce, checks the access token at userinfo, and consumes the ID token once. No pairing code is required.

get.summary: Read bound account identity and device
get.description: The device must belong to the session user; issuer and subject must be bound. This response contains no bearer token.

delete.description: Revokes this session only. Does not erase profile data, other devices, Sync records . Revokes the session ID established by authentication under the shared account lock, including when its token rotates before this handler runs.

post.summary: Issue a short-lived ticket for change notifications
post.description: Requires a native version-2 session bound to an owned device. The ticket is one-use, expires after 30 seconds and replaces any earlier ticket for this session. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Desktop opens the event stream while background Sync is eligible and retains incremental polling as a fallback.

get.description: Authenticate with a one-use notification ticket. The connection sends a heartbeat every 20 seconds and closes after at most 15 minutes. A changed event carries no account ID, collection name or record data; clients must then read the normal Sync feeds. The production nginx route proxies this stream to the dedicated Artisan daemon outside PHP-FPM.

401.description: Missing, expired, reused or invalid notification ticket

get.summary: Read a stable page of encrypted changes
get.description: Start without a cursor. Follow next_cursor until has_more=false to finish the snapshot fence; later writes appear on a later poll. Downloading does not acknowledge. With feature change_page_byte_budget, max_bytes bounds the serialized JSON response, counting escaping and reserving space for metadata/cursors. Default 4 MiB. A byte-limited page may contain fewer than limit records; follow has_more and next_cursor. Clients must also honor record TTL. Session, owned device and bound identity are revalidated under the account lock, including requests admitted before a concurrent session revocation.

200.description: Ordered immutable changes within the snapshot fence

Cache-Control.description: no-store on successful native data responses and protocol errors.

post.summary: Acknowledge durable application of a change page
post.description: Send the received cursor only after all covered records are durably applied or explicitly quarantined. Persist download progress separately when dependencies remain. Repeated or older ACKs cannot reduce the stored position. Session, owned device and bound identity are revalidated under the account lock, including requests admitted before a concurrent session revocation.

Cache-Control.description: no-store on successful native data responses and protocol errors.

post.summary: Apply conditional, idempotent encrypted writes
post.description: Native accounts require an active key and current crypto precondition. Entire JSON body is limited to 4194304 bytes. Each input produces one result; HTTP 200 does not imply every operation succeeded. Preserve UUID and normalized operation exactly across retries. Applied and revision-conflict receipts are durable; quota and invalid outcomes are not cached. A matching old receipt can resolve after key rotation once the request crypto context is refreshed.

Cache-Control.description: no-store on successful native data responses and protocol errors.

get.summary: Read native key state and recovery bundles
get.description: Requires a version-2 session and bound identity. State is created lazily. migration_required is a snapshot; activation rechecks under lock. At most eight keys are retained.

delete.summary: Explicitly erase Sync data and rotate generations
delete.description: Body limit 24576 bytes. Client/transition custody requires authenticated collection_clear controls for all advertised collections, atomically CASing their generations/revisions. Returns 200 and preserves crypto epoch, registry, identity and recovery bundles. Missing controls returns authenticated_control_required. Legacy server custody with crypto alone returns 204, erases bundles and rotates epoch/generations. Clients verify signed controls before local deletion; unsigned resets have no such authority.

Cache-Control.description: Includes no-store; Laravel may also include private.

200.description: Committed result or exact receipt replay

Cache-Control.description: no-store

post.summary: Rotate native session credentials or recover the last rotation
post.description: Renewal proof authenticates this request; no access bearer or cookies are required. User/session/device locks serialize rotation and revocation. Same consumed proof plus same operation returns the exact last receipt; a superseded receipt returns 409. Reuse with another operation revokes that session and all its receipts. Absolute renewal lifetime is 30 days from pairing, never extended. Minimum rotation interval is min(60, floor(access TTL / 2)) seconds; access TTL is clamped to 60–3600 seconds and truncated at absolute renewal expiry. This is the MSP protocol, not a complete OAuth implementation.

requestBody.description: JSON object; at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Unexpected properties are rejected. Proofs must never be sent in query parameters.

200.description: Same session, device, identity and absolute renewal expiration; new access and renewal proofs.

delete.description: Idempotent proof-based revocation, usable after access expiry. The current proof or any retained consumed proof deletes the session and all receipts. Unknown/already-revoked proofs also return 204 without revealing existence. Other sessions and devices are retained. No access bearer is required.

post.summary: Clear synchronized history across devices
post.description: Body limit 24576 bytes. Client/transition custody requires a history_clear control signed by the client identity key; the server validates shape/CAS and retains its opaque proof. Deletes synchronized history and old journal, installs the client generation and cutoff, and stores an exact replay receipt. Missing control returns authenticated_control_required. Old cursors/writes return reset_required plus the current control; clients authenticate before native deletion. Legacy server custody retains its previous unsigned control semantics.

post.description: Atomically CAS both the h1 source and h2 target; target_revision defaults to 0 (absent). Clients fetch/authenticate an existing target, merge content, and send its exact revision. Existing deleted target requires target_deleted true; expired TTL cannot be extended. Source becomes a schema-2 tombstone; target retains deletion or earliest TTL. Source conflict is history_source_conflict; target conflict is history_target_exists when expected absent, otherwise history_target_conflict. Exact replay returns both revisions after completion despite stale crypto revision, with same epoch/device/content. Source replacement first means quota needs only final payload sizes. Any failure rolls back records, changes and receipts. Request limit 600000 UTF-8 bytes.

Read a collision target during active rotation
post.description: Body limit 8192 bytes. Live session, owned device and identity are checked under the account lock. A missing target returns record null. Requires current generation and a rewriting rotation. No secrets are placed in the query string.

post.summary: Replace historical changes with current ciphertext snapshots
post.description: Body limit 24576 bytes. Client custody only. CAS current snapshot_sequence (snapshot_conflict on concurrent change). Every current record must use active schema-2 key, otherwise rotation_records_pending. Preserves generation, record revisions, encrypted tombstones and operation receipts. Changes receive new monotonic sequence numbers. Old cursors explicitly rebase; no local erasure is authorized. Exact replay remains valid after key retirement; changed operation content returns idempotency_conflict.

get.summary: Read the account password encrypted key capsule
get.description: Requires a native session. Returns 409 password_backup_unavailable if no capsule matches the current key IDs and epoch. Cache-Control: no-store. The server never receives the account password.

put.summary: Protect existing Sync keys with the account password locally
put.description: Maximum 65536 UTF-8 request bytes. Validates the session and CAS epoch/revision under the account lock. Requires client custody with no active rotation. Stores ciphertext only; never send password or recovery_secret. Does not change the key registry, revision, identity or data records.

SyncBearer.description: Opaque Sync session token, not an OIDC access token. Store in the profile vault. Native key endpoints require a server-issued version-2 session.

Conflict.description: State conflict. Codes include device_required, native_identity_required, identity_issuer_mismatch, invalid_account_identity, reset_required, crypto_state_conflict, native_keys_required, native_keys_already_active, legacy_migration_required, incompatible_devices, key_id_exists, key_capacity_reached, key_version_exhausted and revision_exhausted. Preserve pending data and reconcile; never infer a lost write failed from a conflict. Native pairing may also return native_session_required or refresh_session_capacity without consuming its code.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded. Honor Retry-After; the framework response is not a Sync protocol error.

Counter.description: Decimal counter, carried as a string to avoid JavaScript rounding.

Revision.description: Decimal CAS revision. Stored record/key-state revisions cannot exceed 2147483647.

Cursor.description: Opaque authenticated server token bound to account, device, collection and generation. Never parse or manufacture it.

RecordId.description: Opaque collection record ID. Native non-deleted records additionally forbid control characters and are limited to 255 UTF-8 bytes.

KeyId.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of exactly 16 bytes.

issuer.description: Exact configured OIDC issuer, including trailing slash. Explicit local mode uses urn:midori:sync:local.

encrypted_bundle.description: JSON text of the V2 recovery envelope, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes. Exact fields: bundle_version=2, crypto_version=2, key_id, kdf (argon2id13, memory_kib=65536, iterations=3, parallelism=1), salt (16 bytes), nonce (24 bytes), ciphertext (48 bytes); binary fields use canonical padded base64. The client must verify AEAD, account scope and recoverability.

registry_auth_version.description: Version 2 authenticates the resulting crypto revision in the key-registry MAC. Omission in requests is legacy version 1; a version-2 registry cannot downgrade.

password_unlock.description: True when a password-encrypted key capsule matches the current epoch and key IDs. False after key rotation until an unlocked client replaces the capsule. Optional on older servers.

pairing_token.description: Secret, single-use pairing code. Store neither the code nor this response in logs.

expires_in.description: Validity in seconds; configured server-side, 300 by default.

native_refresh.description: Explicit opt-in. Omission never issues a renewable credential.

token.description: Opaque bearer secret. Never log it.

device_types.description: Supported browser authorization device types. Omission means desktop only. The type is bound to the grant at authorization time.

data_schemas.description: Highest client capability generation per collection, not a value to copy into plaintext version. Bookmarks and history use plaintext version 1 with generation 2; tabs publishes version 2. midori-privacy generation 1 requires custom_filters and covers custom filter text only. site-permissions generation 1 requires site_permissions and covers portable site blocks and exceptions, never sensitive grants. The server stores ciphertext only.

payload.description: Opaque ciphertext, including schema-2 tombstones. Only legacy tombstones have an empty payload. Clients authenticate deleted/ttl inside the plaintext wrapper before applying metadata.

snapshot_rebased.description: An older cursor was rebased to current-record snapshots after compaction. Never authorizes local deletion.

payload.description: V2 envelope binding collection/id/generation/base_revision and schema 2 in client/transition custody (schema 1 for server custody). Schema 2 is mandatory even for deletions and encrypts {version:2,deleted,ttl,value}; payload must not be empty. Server validates public metadata, never AEAD plaintext.

anyOf.description: Expiration is normalized to UTC whole seconds; clients must also enforce TTL before server cleanup runs.

registry_auth_version.description: Version 2 authenticates the resulting crypto revision in the key-registry MAC. Omission in requests is legacy version 1; a version-2 registry cannot downgrade.

WipeRequest.description: Client/transition custody requires operation_id and one collection_clear control for every advertised collection; legacy server custody may use crypto alone.

salt.description: Canonical padded base64 of exactly 16 bytes; server also checks canonical padding bits.

nonce.description: Canonical padded base64 of exactly 24 bytes; server also checks canonical padding bits.

ciphertext.description: Canonical padded base64 of exactly 48 bytes; server also checks canonical padding bits.

nonce.description: Canonical padded base64 of exactly 24 bytes; server also checks canonical padding bits.

ciphertext.description: Canonical padded base64 encoding of 16–190016 bytes, including the AEAD tag. The server checks decoded length and canonical padding.

RefreshToken.description: Opaque renewal proof, distinct from the access bearer. Never log it or place it in a URL.

RefreshOperationId.description: Persist before sending. Repeat the same ID after an uncertain response; the server returns it in lowercase.

token.description: Opaque bearer secret. Never log it.

RefreshResponse.description: Exact response from the committed rotation. A recovered response may have expired access credentials: durably store its new refresh proof, then rotate again with a new persisted operation ID before using protected APIs. expires_in describes the original issuance time, not the replay time.

clear_before.description: UTC cutoff; visits at or before this millisecond must not be uploaded again.

HistoryClearMarker.description: Compatibility projection of history clear cutoff. In client/transition custody it must match the authenticated control exactly, including milliseconds; this marker alone has no authority.

HistoryClearRequest.description: control is required for client/transition custody. Its previous_generation and operation_id must match the outer fields.

RegistryAuth.description: Opaque lowercase hexadecimal MAC with the independent identity key. Version 2 signs ["MidoriSync/key-registry/v2", epoch, resulting revision as a decimal string, active_key_id, identity_key, sorted data keys, custody, server_recovery, stableRotation]. Each new crypto mutation signs current revision + 1. Version 1 omits revision for legacy compatibility.

registry_auth_version.description: Version 2 authenticates the resulting crypto revision in the key-registry MAC. Omission in requests is legacy version 1; a version-2 registry cannot downgrade.

target_ttl.description: For live target, the earliest non-null current source/target TTL, UTC whole seconds, including expired values. For target_deleted true, null. Authenticated payload must match.

control_revision.description: CAS current control revision + 1, at most 9007199254740991.

clear_before_ms.description: Positive UTC milliseconds for history_clear; exactly 0 for collection_clear.

AuthenticatedControl.description: Client MAC using identity devices subkey over JSON ["MidoriSync/control/v1",epoch,collection,operation_id,previous_generation,generation,control_revision,kind,clear_before_ms]. Server stores the tag opaquely. Receivers must verify it and anchored revision before destructive local actions.

payload.description: Native crypto v2 purpose=local envelope, browser-settings/sync-password-backup-v1, generation=crypto epoch, schema_version=1, base_revision=0. Ciphertext protects at most 32768 plaintext bytes; see native-sync-api.md.
